title: COMMENT ON Implement 0L04 Gradient Calibration results (Execution date specified by Ops)
body/content: Per discussions with Injector group, we'll aim to do this when Hall C goes to 5th pass and required a laser frequency change. Sometime in the next 2-3 weeks, extrapolating from NPES schedule, is when that will happen (after 4th pass running).

title: COMMENT ON RF 2.0 C100 Software Update - Support new power limit calculations & algorithm optimizations
body/content:
From task author: plan is to test the algorithm in 2L22 and then propagate the software to the other C100 zones (the other zones may happen on another maintenance day). The new software will provide an easy way to open the klystron power limits. As Hall C moves to 4th pass up to ~70uA, this will give AESRF another knob for tweaking how much headroom we allocate for gradient, detuning and beam loading. 

This work is approved to occur today. Added to SAM Cal.

title: Hall C Dumplette gold mask set to masked when destination not set to C
body/content: When pausing beam to check orbits and path length, we noticed that inserting the Hall C dumplette did not trip FSD. Checking the tree, it was found that with the destination masked to Halls B and D, the gold mask for the Hall C dumplette was set to masked. Checking back through previous destination masking, this seems to be occurring whenever Hall C is not included in the masking, but it's not immediately obvious to me when this started occurring because the masking PV is a combination of every state on the node. Figures 1-3 show masking state at the time the issue was noticed and anomalies. Not shown on the anomalies screen are all the masked BLMs, which are hopefully irrelevant.

title: COMMENT ON Test bleedThrough4.0
body/content:
Tested the script today: https://logbooks.jlab.org/entry/4516824

A few notes:

The script will not open the slits fully for the measurement. It seems it will only go between the slit values that were present when the script was started and the fully closed value. Perhaps this is intended as it can also be used to measure bleedthrough with beam into a hall.

When taking the first bleedthrough measurement, it started to collect bleedthrough data for the C slit before the A and B slits were fully closed. This didn't seem to be a problem on subsequent measurements.

title: Picoammeter Backgrounds vs Range Check
body/content: As was requested by an injector SME, I checked the picoammeter background readings before and after the bleedthrough script testing. I plotted the PV that the script should be paying attention to (FCupsCORRECTED.VAL) and the FCupsrange PV, and proceeded to work my way up the range settings from to 200 uA. All appears to behave as I expect; the background measurement is very repeatable and consistent across the ranges up to the 2 uA setting when the  last pA digit drops off. So long as we aren't measuring above 200 nA of bleedthrough, we should be good!

title: bleedThrough4.0 Testing
body/content:
The shared-slit situation appears to be handled gracefully and, though I could only test the permutation currently available in the injector, I would hope the logic behaves properly for any possible situation. Figure 2 shows the liveplot of beam modes, slit positions, and the current measured at FC1 throughout all the non-Quick-Check measurements. Figure 3 shows the same but for the measurement with all halls selected. I was curious if 5 seconds would be enough for a stable measurement, but it seems fine enough from this view. I believe the picoammeter readback is an average of the past 10 samples anyhow. I'll touch base with Riad to determine if this is sufficient for our measurements. 

The biggest issue appears to be that the tool is not actually reporting any current when FC1 is definitely measuring it. I am not sure what the tool monitors, but the correct PV would be FCupsCORRECTED.VAL as far as I am aware.

The error about setting slits manually happens due to the B slit taking a long time to move all the way to the target position or due to the position readbacks having some degree of error. I would suggest upping the timeout to a minute and adding a +/- 0.1mm tolerance window for position.

Closing the "Enter Nominal Current" dialog without entering a value (or perhaps closing it at all) causes the tool to get stuck. 

Input sanitization may be a good idea, though it doesn't seem to screw up anything but the percentage calculations which we can get rid of anyways.

It took me by surprise that when Quick Check is selected the script resumes CW to the hall when it was not initially on, so I would suggest at least opening a dialog to confirm it is okay to send back before doing so. It also seems to produce duplicate log entries.

Figure 4 shows the terminal output for all the tests.

title: COMMENT ON Update to SCAM Controls on iocin1
body/content:
Just wanted to follow up on this discussion... 

The BOOM Buddy PVs are there so that the software knows which lasers are intended to go through which slits and to which Halls. It is an intentional flag that is set, so the software knows the intended combination. BOOM Buddy itself does not protect anything. The SCAM controls prevent the selection of CW to a laser that do not have an intended chopper slit selected in BOOM Buddy. This logic is currently ignored if the In Line Dump is in. With the new logic, the BOOM Buddy logic will be ignored if the PCup, FCup1, FCup2, or ILD is in. Max is correct that there is no hazard when the device is inserted on an FSD trip and beam is dumped in the device and the laser turns off. The issue is, upon restoration of the Beam Trip. Usually, lasers are restored, normally using the EASY Button, then the FCup is pulled. So, while the FCup is inserted an Operator could select CW without an issue to a laser that doesn't have an intended Boom Buddy laser path set. As soon as the FCup is pulled out, it would trip the laser mode and then deny the request until one of the 4 devices are reinserted. 

It is possible I am over thinking this, but I wanted to raise this as an possible issue and have others accept/ approve this logic.

body/content: After looking at the code some more, I have thought of an unintended consequence of this new logic. On every FSD trip either FCup2 or FCup is inserted. This means that the Boom Buddy PVs will be ignored briefly every FSD trip.  There are additional protections, as soon as the device is removed the software will trip the laser and not allow you to select CW, until the FCups are reinserted and the logic is ignored again. Another protection is that mostly the Easy Button is used after a trip, so it usually will restore what ever we are running prior to the FSD trip. Please let me know if we need to rethink this new logic?

So, this should have only been the case for 4 electrometers:  NDX1L24, NDX1S01,  NDX2L24, NDX2S01 

I also found that the CED configuration for type NDX_Electrometer has several incorrect elements. This however did not seem to hurt the system in any way. I will work on fixing this too.

title: COMPLETED Validate harp abort behavior in qsUtility for Semi-Automatic mode harp scans
body/content: Validated the resetHarp abort path on IHA3E01 and IHA4E01 during maintenance. Confirmed that adding a two-second delay between setMode and abortAndReset reliably retracts the harp. Plan is to update qsUtility with the delay and add a status/OUT-limit verification dialog. Will investigate adding an additional alarm for the harps that are neither at the IN or OUT limit and put masks inside of qsUtility.

title: qsUtility harp abort/retract testing on IHA3E01 and IHA4E01
body/content:
Tested the qsUtility resetHarp behavior on two operational harps during today's maintenance window to validate findings from earlier bench testing. Confirmed that the current resetHarp ordering (setMode followed immediately by abortAndReset) can leave the harp mid-travel because the ABORT write interrupts the retract that the mode change just initiated. Tried swapping the order so abortAndReset runs before setMode, but this produced inconsistent behavior and occasionally left the harp inserted. The reproducible fix was adding a two-second delay between setMode and abortAndReset, which retracted the harp cleanly on every iteration across both IHA3E01 and IHA4E01.

Plans to add the delay to qsUtility's resetHarp. Also investigating a follow-up dialog in qsUtility to display the current harp scan status and confirm the harp is at the OUT limit before declaring the reset complete, so any future failure to retract is surfaced to the user rather than silently leaving the harp inserted.

Special thanks to Dennis from CASA for assisting with the troubleshooting and implementation.

title: Follow-up Re: Follow-up Re: QuickPic - Adding New Matrix Lock to Generic Locks Killed Lock Server?
body/content:
I am still investigating the cause of the initial crash.

The inability to restart was fallout from a procedural error made when the lock server was ported to RHEL9. When the Generic Locks server was ported to opsbat9 a few months ago, a patch to the PIOC sponsor library was required. In the rush to complete the test plan, I inadvertently left a version of the GenericLocks installed that was pointing at the dvl version of the PIOC. Subsequent changes to the dvl version of the PIOC sponsor library to address a different problem left it in an inconsistent state. When the Generic Locks server restarted, it got the incompatible version of the PIOC sponsor library. This left the lock server unable to communicate with the PIOC server. An old bug in the sponsor library caused the lock server to exhaust its file descriptors (1024 per process, apparently) trying to connect to the PIOC. I found and fixed that bug before I found the bug that was making it fail to communicate. With that old bug fixed I was able to restart the lock server such that it was still not sponsoring new PVs on the PIOC, but it didn't run out of file descriptors and so could carry out its primary function. I subsequently found the new bug (actually a testing feature) that was preventing the servers from communicating, but I refrained from restarting the lock server again since it had already been down for so long.

The current state is that the lock server is functioning except that it can't create new PVs on the PIOC for new locks. This will be fixed when I deploy a new build of the lock server that doesn't use the dvl version of the PIOC sponsor library. Hopefully that build will also contain a fix for the bug that caused the server to crash on creation of a new matrix lock. Note that the new matrix lock was successfully created once the server was back up and running.

title: Unacknowledgable VIP2I02A HV alarm (again)
body/content: Looks like the same thing happened where the alarm's .ACKS field went INVALID and thus could not be acknowledged by Ops. Disabling then reenabling the alarm node did the trick of resetting the node to green again. Leaving this OPS-PR open since it seems like there may be an underlying problem other than the injector alarm handler needing a restart.

title: Unable to acknowledge VIP2I02A alarm
body/content: Alarm appears to be a false positive, given the steady readbacks. The alarm would not acknowlege for anyone in the control room, though, so contacted software on call for assistance in silencing the beeps.

body/content:
OPS reported that signals from iocse20 aren't appearing in myaplot after the IOC was rebooted.

Using IPM3H07A as an example signal.

It's available in EPICS

[63] theo@opsl90 > camonitor IPM3H07A.XPOS
IPM3H07A.XPOS                  2026-05-05 21:14:40.323452 1.80363  
IPM3H07A.XPOS                  2026-05-05 21:14:43.306785 1.8293  
IPM3H07A.XPOS                  2026-05-05 21:14:46.306785 1.76872  

However mya hasn't seen it reconnect in over an hour.  

2026-05-05 19:39:29 1.83365
2026-05-05 19:39:32 1.84865
2026-05-05 19:39:36 1.74715
2026-05-05 19:40:12 << Network disconnection >>

I think this is a case now that doesn't involve the Hall D gateway, so that may have been a red herring.  This will need further investigation.


I tried deactivating and reactivating it in mya, but that didn't produce any effect. In fact from the log file, it appears mya ignored my explicit commands:

[mya@opsmya0 ~]$ bin/active -s 0 IPM3H07A.XPOS
[mya@opsmya0 ~]$ bin/active -s 1 IPM3H07A.XPOS

[2026-05-05 21:08:40] Channel actions: 0 Enabled, 0 Disabled, 1 Ignored {Normal}.

title: COMMENT ON make harp speed uniform
body/content:
Set all harp scan speeds to 1.5 mm/sec by writing to both the O and SCANO PVs for each harp. SCANO is part of the myRestore set for the harp IOCs. So whatever was last recorded by the archiver, that is what's set after an IOC reboot/restore. 11 harps timed out and are not currently available on the network:

IHA1C07B, IHA1C18A, IHA1C18B, IHA1H00, IHA1H04A, IHA1H04B, IHA1P02, IHA2A21, IHA4D00E, IHAAT05, IHATS01

Some additional information. The PV you enter on the expert screen for velocity, <HarpName>SCANO, does not write directly to hardware the way the acceleration and deceleration PVs do. It holds the requested velocity until a scan is commanded. Then the sequencer updates the hardware PV. This matters because if you abort a scan mid-travel, the velocity is set to zero. On the next scan the IOC picks up the value you entered on the screen, not the zero that was last sent to hardware. Also, once the harp hits the IN limit switch it reverses and retracts at maximum velocity so you are not waiting around.

title: iocsb4 BELS Restored
body/content:
I&C came in to assist with the IP-Octal module issue. Initial replacement of the module in Slot 0 allowed the board to be addressed in software, but as soon as any serial query was sent to the PLC, the card generated an interrupt storm causing kernel work queue overflow.

I&C then reinstalled the original board to verify the system could still boot. After reseating, the original board was now addressable (previously it was not detected at all), but exhibited the same kernel panic behavior as the replacement.

To isolate the issue, both ribbon cables connecting to the serial breakout panel were disconnected. After a reboot with the cables removed, the IOC came up cleanly and was able to address both Module 0 and Module 1 without kernel panic.

The ribbon cables were then reconnected and the system came up normally and was able to communicate with the PLCs without the interrupt storm.

Operations was informed and was able to clear the BELS faults. System is now operational.

Special thanks to James Donaldson from I&C for his assistance.

title: iocsb4 BELS PLC Comm Errors
body/content:
Software On-Call was contacted regarding two issues with iocsb4. Some restoration failures and BELS PLC communication errors.

The restoration issue was caused by PVs in the restore set that are not yet archived. These have been temporarily disabled and the IOC was successfully restored. Will follow-up with the SMEs. 

For the BELS PLC errors, I compared the April 13 console log to previous successful boots from March 25 and February 24. In the working logs, BelInit successfully opened serial ports /tyGS/0/0/0 and /tyGS/0/0/4. On April 13, BelInit failed with "Could not open ports."

The boot log shows the IP-Octal module in Carrier 0, Slot 0 is not being detected. The ipacReport output shows "No IPAC ID" for Slot 0. This caused the tyGSOctalModuleInit for Mod0 to fail, which prevented the serial ports from being created.

Working with Ops on a reseat of the board and a VME crate power cycle to attempt recovery. I&C will need to be contacted if the IP-Octal module has failed. SSG was contacted as well to check the health of the PLCs.

title: Beam Mode Limitation Due to Hall A Power Work
body/content:
When iochla went offline due to power work in Hall A, three insertables lost status, causing the Insertable Manager server to limit the beam mode to Viewer Limited. We initially suspected ITV3H10 based on server logs, but temporarily unpowering it in the CED ruled it out and confirmed the issue was with the Hall A viewers. To resolve the issue, ITV10D00A, IOR1H04A, and IDP10D00 were set to unpowered in the CED, and the Insertable Manager server was restarted.

Special thanks to Ops, I&C, and the CED Admins for their support.

title: Radiation monitor comms + Hall C Dump radiation monitor update
body/content:
Two unique problems, but put condensing them into one log for clarity

-Hall C Dump radiation monitor alarm
Figures 1-3: Upon taking Hall C's current up to 35 uA, a major alarm came in for RM702. According to RadCon, this only means the magenta beacon outside Building 95 (the dump service building) will be flashing. Since there are no plans to access this building any time soon, we can safely continue running with this alarm. There is currently a Comm error blinking in and out, but it's updating every few minutes at least. iocsoftrad2 may need a reboot, but it can wait until Monday.

-iocrad1 CARM Comm issue
Figures 4-9: A little before noon today, a bunch of CARMs in the west halls including a couple in the counting house lost communications and stopped updating but didn't throw an alarm (figure 6). All of these monitors are on iocrad1, which is reporting okay, but one ioc issue sounds more likely than a dozen CARMs individually failing at the same time. As it stands, this is not interfering with beam delivery, and we have the okay from RadCon to leave it as-is until system experts can look at it Monday. However, if a hall needs to make an access before then, there's a chance we will get stuck in Power Permit because one of the CARMs, #31 Hall C Transport Tunnel, is PSS-interlocked and showing red on the iFix screen. In that case, we will attempt a local reset of iocrad1 and hope it reestablishes communications.
